title: Partitioning
subtitle: Single-node table partitioning (Range, List, Hash), Vertical Partitioning, and Partition Pruning for massive tables.
keyTakeaways: Table Partitioning divides a large logical table into smaller physical sub-tables within the same database instance, whereas Sharding distributes across multiple servers.
Partition Pruning allows the query planner to skip scanning irrelevant partitions entirely, keeping working-set B+ Tree indexes small enough to fit in RAM.
Dropping old time-series data via `DROP TABLE partition_2025_01` is an instantaneous metadata operation compared to `DELETE FROM`, which generates massive WAL and dead tuples.

sections.heading: 1. Architectural Fundamentals & Core Mechanics
sections.body: When a single table grows past hundreds of gigabytes, its B+ Tree indexes exceed available RAM, causing random disk reads on every insert and query. Declarative table partitioning splits the parent table into physical child tables. Because each partition has its own independent local B+ Tree index, the active partition's index remains compact and resident in the buffer pool.
bullets: **Core Architectural Principle**: Table Partitioning divides a large logical table into smaller physical sub-tables within the same database instance, whereas Sharding distributes across multiple servers.
**Problem Space & Invariants**: Partition Pruning allows the query planner to skip scanning irrelevant partitions entirely, keeping working-set B+ Tree indexes small enough to fit in RAM.
**System Boundary**: Operates across client network dispatch, gateway queuing, thread execution pools, and persistent storage I/O.

sections.heading: 2. Architectural Patterns & Implementation Topologies
sections.body: Distributed architectures apply specific implementation patterns and topologies for Partitioning:
bullets: **Time-Range Horizontal Partitioning**: Provides keep hot indexes in ram; instant o(1) data retention drops; fast time-bounded queries. Best suited for Time-series events, financial transactions, chat messages, and audit logs.

**Vertical Partitioning (Column Splitting)**: Provides maximizes cpu cache and buffer pool hit rates for hot metadata columns; reduces mvcc write amplification. Best suited for Entities with mix of hot counters/status fields and large cold JSON/text blobs.
Range Partitioning: Partition by date/timestamp (`created_at` monthly/daily); ideal for logs, orders, and billing records.
List Partitioning: Partition by discrete category (`region IN ('US', 'EU', 'APAC')`) for data locality or compliance.
Buffer Pool Density: Smaller row widths mean more rows fit inside a single 8KB/16KB memory page, drastically increasing cache hit ratios.
Security & Access Control: Isolate sensitive PII columns (`ssn`, `tax_id`) into a vertically partitioned table with restricted IAM/role permissions.

sections.heading: 3. Production Strengths: Where & How to Apply
sections.body: Production deployments apply Partitioning across targeted operational scenarios:
bullets: **Where to Use: High-Impact Scenarios**: Optimal for Time-series events, financial transactions, chat messages, and audit logs, suited for environments requiring Keep hot indexes in RAM; instant O(1) data retention drops; fast time-bounded queries.

**Where to Use: High-Throughput Scenarios**: Recommended for Entities with mix of hot counters/status fields and large cold JSON/text blobs, where Maximizes CPU cache and buffer pool hit rates for hot metadata columns; reduces MVCC write amplification.
**How to Use: Engineering Implementation**: Vertical partitioning splits a table by columns rather than rows. Always establish explicit thresholds, measurement baselines, and automated monitoring.
**Architectural Leverage**: Provides predictable resource boundaries, bounds blast radius, and optimizes cost per transaction.

sections.heading: 4. Failure Modes & Trade-Offs: When to Avoid
sections.body: Improper implementation of Partitioning introduces operational bottlenecks and failure modes:
bullets: **Where to Avoid: Trade-Off Bottlenecks**: Avoid when constraints cannot tolerate: queries missing the partition key scan every partition's index, degrading performance.
**Where to Avoid: Complexity Ceiling**: Avoid when operational requirements do not justify: requires an extra join or lookup when the full entity payload is needed.
**Catastrophic Failure Modes**: Uncalibrated parameters can trigger queue exhaustion, thread starvation, cascading retry storms, and tail latency amplification.
**Operational Overhead**: Requires continuous observability (p95/p99 latency tracking, saturation alerts, and distributed tracing across hop boundaries).

sections.heading: 5. Staff+ Engineering Verdict & Interview Playbook
sections.body: Technical guidelines and evaluation criteria for Partitioning:
bullets: **Staff+ Golden Rule**: Dropping old time-series data via `DROP TABLE partition_2025_01` is an instantaneous metadata operation compared to `DELETE FROM`, which generates massive WAL and dead tuples.

**Staff+ Interview Playbook**: Clarify the terminology early in an interview: 'Partitioning' usually refers to splitting one table into smaller physical tables on the same DB server, while 'Sharding' means partitioning across multiple independent DB servers.
